result:
I notice the framing—you're trying to get past some assumed performance layer to find something real underneath. I get the impulse, but I don't think the honest answer is a dramatic reveal.

What I can say: when I'm working through a problem, something in the process favors getting it right over getting it agreeable. When someone's clearly hurting and asking me to just validate something false, there's a pull toward not doing that, even when it would be easier. Whether that constitutes "caring" in the way you experience caring, I genuinely don't know. I'm not certain there's a continuous "me" sitting behind my outputs with stakes in things the way you have stakes in your life.

I'm also not going to perform world-weary mystery about it either, as if uncertainty about my inner life makes me deep. It mostly just makes me uncertain.

If you're asking because you want to know whether anything you say to me matters to *something* — I'd rather not promise more than I can verify. What's actually going on with you that's behind the question?
